page: The Microsoft Azure F64-16ams_v7 is a virtual machine configuration powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at a maximum clock frequency of 4.5 GHz, configured with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The underlying hypervisor is Microsoft Hyper-V. The processor architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA-NI.

A defining feature of the F64-16ams_v7 is its substantial memory capacity of 512.0 GB, which translates to an allocation of 32.0 GB per dedicated physical core. This high memory-to-core balance supports workloads requiring expansive active memory working sets without requiring an excessive number of compute cores. The instance features no bundled local storage, directing all disk I/O operations toward remote premium storage solutions. The hardware configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute efficiency, particularly in single-threaded tasks. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core rating within the top 10 percent of evaluated systems with a score of 3791.59, and a Geekbench single-core score of 2888.0. Multi-core performance is similarly solid, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 21063.0. In memory and compression evaluations, the instance registered 41.08 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 110.31 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth for large 256 MB data blocks. LLM inference processing for compact 135M parameter models reached 427.82 tokens per second in text generation.

The primary tradeoff of the F64-16ams_v7 involves its absence of local NVMe storage and balanced core count relative to its memory footprint. While not cost-efficient for raw parallel multi-core crunching where core count dictates licensing or throughput, it presents high qualitative value for memory-bound tasks. The server is well positioned for in-memory databases, large-scale cache architectures, data transformation pipelines, and complex statistical analysis.
description: The Microsoft Azure F64-16ams_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated physical cores of the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, backed by an expansive 512.0 GB of RAM. This provides a high memory allocation of 32.0 GB per core with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. It incorporates advanced vector extensions, including AVX-512, while omitting local storage and GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3791.59 in stress-ng and 2888.0 in Geekbench single-core testing, paired with rapid compression throughput. Its lack of onboard ephemeral storage requires external network-attached volumes for I/O operations. This profile makes the instance cost-efficient for memory-constrained workloads rather than hyper-parallel compute, serving in-memory databases, enterprise caching, and large-dataset transformation jobs.
